message.content:
Taking “the last few months” as **August–November 8, 2026**, these are the clearest recent launches and substantial updates I could verify. They cover different needs: API spend attribution, broader AI FinOps, and cost-aware observability.

| Tool | Launch or major-release date | What’s new and relevant | Important distinction |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Anthropic Usage and Cost Analytics API** | **October 29, 2026 — beta launch** | New endpoints report token usage and costs, with filtering/grouping by model, workspace, API key, and user or service account. | **Claude-only, API-first**, rather than a cross-provider dashboard. The older Usage and Cost API remains supported but is now legacy. ([platform.claude.com](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview?entry=september-28-2026&utm_source=openai)) |
| **CloudKeeper — Full Stack FinOps for AI** | **October 27, 2026 — launch** | Unified tracking of model/inference spend, token usage, AI licenses, cloud infrastructure, and GPU costs/utilization; consolidates AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud data. | Broader **enterprise AI cost management**, not just per-request API tracking. The announcement offers a 30-day trial. ([cloudkeeper.com](https://www.cloudkeeper.com/newsroom/press-release/cloudkeeper-makes-aillm-cost-tracking-easier-businesses-full-stack-finops-ai)) |
| **FiscaLLM** | **Mid-October 2026 — initial release, according to its developer** | Connects AI usage costs to subscription revenue to show **margin per user and plan**, with budget alerts and optional spend caps. Open-source, self-hostable, with TypeScript and Python SDKs. | An early-stage independent project. On October 23, the developer said it had shipped “a week ago”; that establishes an approximate release window, not an exact launch day. ([reddit.com](https://www.reddit.com/r/buildinpublic/comments/1xd00qd/week_1_building_in_public_shipped_an_opensource/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Honeycomb — AI Ecosystem** | **September 29, 2026 — early-access announcement** | Introduces **LLM Cost Tracking**, Agent Fleet Performance, and Agent Conversations, connecting fleet-wide token usage/cost signals to individual conversations. | Primarily **production observability with cost tracking**. The announcement described early access, with general availability anticipated at year-end or early the following year—not a confirmed GA launch. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/honeycomb-unveils-new-ai-observability-features-to-close-the-gap-between-shipping-agents-and-understanding-them-302892466.html)) |
| **Mizan — Router, Analyst, and optimization update** | **September 1, 2026 — major-update announcement** | Expanded routing across 150+ models and 10+ providers; project-scoped keys, separate budgets, and per-call cost telemetry. Analyst adds direct-provider usage syncing and subscription-receipt ingestion. | Combines **gateway-based tracking and broader spend aggregation**, including spend that never passes through its router. This is an expansion of an existing product, not a first launch. ([try-mizan.com](https://www.try-mizan.com/blog/major-mizan-updates)) |

**The most useful distinction:** FiscaLLM focuses on whether individual customers are profitable; Mizan on cross-provider routing and spend attribution; CloudKeeper on the overall organizational AI bill; Honeycomb on connecting costs to agent behavior; and Anthropic’s new API on extracting Claude-native usage and cost data. ([github.com](https://github.com/magna56/fiscallm))

This is a **verified shortlist, not an exhaustive market census**. I’ve separated first launches, major updates, and beta/early-access announcements so they aren’t mistaken for equivalent release milestones.
